title: Splitting the flock
_map: Lesson map: Splitting the flock (Y1–2). Big idea: number bonds, 10 can be split into two parts in set ways.
_stepChain: counting → a flock of 10 sheep → two fields → split them any way → every split still makes 10 → the pairs that make 10 are called number bonds → the pattern: one side goes up as the other goes down

talk.ask: How many ways can 10 sheep go into two fields?
talk.goodAnswer: 11 ways, from 0 and 10 up to 10 and 0. Every way still makes 10.

talk.ask: When one field gets one more sheep, what happens to the other field?
talk.goodAnswer: it gets one fewer, so the total stays 10.

handsOn: Take 10 Lego bricks and two bowls. Find every way to share them between the bowls, and line the ways up in order. What pattern do you see?

narration.text: The farm has 10 sheep, and two fields of fresh grass. The sheep can go into either field. Some can go here, and some can go there.
Choose how many sheep go into the first field, then tap the hammer. The rest go into the other field. How many different ways can you find?

Every single way still makes 10 sheep. 4 and 6. 7 and 3. 0 and 10. Pairs of numbers that make 10 like this are called number bonds. Look at your list: when one field gets one more sheep, the other field gets one fewer.
Now imagine a bigger flock: 20 sheep.

question.prompt: How many ways can 20 sheep go into two fields? Make a guess.
question.reveal: 21 ways! From 0 and 20, all the way to 20 and 0. With 10 sheep there were 11 ways; with 20 sheep there are 21. Always one more than the number of sheep.

rule.text: Split 10 any way: the parts still make 10.
rule.ask: Can you say what stays the same, however you split the sheep? Say it out loud. Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: However you split 10, the two parts still make 10. Those pairs are called number bonds.

bonus.prompt: Bonus: what if there were three fields? Guess how many ways 10 sheep could go into three fields.
bonus.reveal: 66 ways! Adding one more field makes lots more ways. That's a puzzle mathematicians love.
